title: Web Development in Chicago, IL | 22 Signals
description: Web development for Chicago firms: redesigns, migrations that keep rankings, client portals and e-commerce for law firms, manufacturers and food brands.
h1: Web development for Chicago firms that have outgrown their site
intro: We do web development for established Chicago companies whose website no longer matches the business: redesigns, CMS rebuilds, migrations that keep your Google rankings, e-commerce and secure client portals. Typical clients are Loop law and accounting firms, suburban manufacturers, distributors and food brands. You get a faster site that brings in inquiries, built and looked after by one team.

p: Plenty of Chicago companies run on a website built for a different version of the business. The product catalog lives in PDFs. The careers page lists roles filled two years ago. The CMS needs a plugin update nobody dares to run. Meanwhile buyers check the site before every call, and so do the AI assistants they ask for recommendations.

A rebuild is the obvious answer, but the risk is real: a careless relaunch can wipe out rankings that took years to earn. Good web development. Chicago firms need a rebuild that protects what already works and fixes what does not.

list: Website rebuilds and redesigns with clear service pages, fast load times and accessible design.
Migrations that keep rankings: URL mapping, redirects, metadata and content carried across, then checked after launch.
CMS setups your marketing team can actually edit, on WordPress or a headless CMS.
E-commerce for brands and distributors, including B2B ordering and account pricing.
Client portals with secure logins, document sharing and payments.
Website care and security: updates, backups, uptime monitoring and fixes.

sections.h: Choosing a partner for web development: Chicago red flags
p: We hear the same stories from Chicago firms that had a bad rebuild. Avoid them by watching for a few warning signs when you compare quotes for web development. Chicago buyers should be wary of:
list: No plan for redirects, or a shrug when you ask what happens to your current rankings.
A design presented before anyone has asked what your sales team needs from the site.
A proprietary CMS that only the agency can edit.
No mention of security updates, backups or who looks after the site after launch.
Accounts, domains and hosting set up in the agency's name instead of yours.

sections.h: Proof: a client portal for a US law firm
p: We built a client portal for a US law firm where clients log in, see their documents and pay invoices in one place. The firm's staff stopped emailing files back and forth, and clients stopped calling to ask for copies. Chicago firms with heavy document traffic, in law, accounting or insurance, are a natural fit for the same approach.

Every contact form, portal and checkout collects personal information, and the Illinois Personal Information Protection Act expects reasonable security for it. We use encrypted connections, store only what you need, restrict admin access and keep software patched, because outdated plugins are the usual way small business sites in Chicago and everywhere else get hacked.
If your site or portal would use face matching for ID checks or voice features, BIPA applies, and we plan written consent and retention rules before launch or recommend a different approach.

p: Chicago clients see design and build work on a staging site between reviews, so each review call has something new to look at. Calls are arranged at times that suit your team, and feedback is collected in one shared list. Launches are scheduled for your low-traffic hours and checked page by page afterwards.
One Signal Lead runs the project and owns the timeline. If a workshop in Chicago with your partners or leadership would speed up sign-off, we plan a visit when the project needs it.

faqs.q: Will a new website hurt our Google rankings?
faqs.a: Not if the migration is handled properly. We map every old URL to a new one, set redirects, carry over titles and content that rank, and check rankings and errors after launch. Most ranking drops after a Chicago site relaunch come from skipped redirects or deleted pages, and both are preventable.

faqs.q: Do you build websites for Chicago law firms?
faqs.a: Yes. Law firms are one of our most experienced sectors. We build practice area pages, attorney profiles and intake forms, plus secure client portals with documents and payments. We also handle security for law firm sites, including clean-ups after a site has been compromised, which is more common than most firms think.

faqs.q: Can you build B2B ordering for a Chicago distributor?
faqs.a: Yes. We build B2B shops with customer accounts, account-specific pricing, quick reorder and quote requests, connected to your ERP or inventory system where possible. For Chicago distributors serving the Midwest, that usually means fewer phone and email orders for your inside sales team to key in by hand.

Mostly WordPress for marketing sites, because it is widely known and easy for teams to edit, and a headless CMS when a site needs more speed or custom features. We recommend based on who will edit the site and what it must connect to. Either way, your team gets training and full access.

faqs.q: Do you meet Chicago clients in person?
faqs.a: When it helps, yes. Most web projects run well on video reviews and a staging site you can click through at any time. If a kick-off or content workshop with your leadership would help, we plan a visit to Chicago when the project needs it.

faqs.q: Do you look after the site after launch?
faqs.a: Yes. Website care covers updates, backups, uptime and security monitoring, small changes and performance checks. Outdated plugins and weak passwords are the most common way sites get hacked, so regular care matters as much as the build. Many clients also keep us on for SEO and content.

faqs.q: How long does a website rebuild take?
faqs.a: It depends on the number of pages, the content and the integrations. A focused marketing site takes less time than a large catalog or a site with a client portal. For web development, Chicago firms with partner or board sign-off should plan time for approvals as well as the build. We agree the timeline and review dates in writing at the planning stage.
